full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J.: This rule is directed against the order dated 18.7.96 passed by the learned 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Noagaon in Misc. Case. No. 91 of 1994 dismissing the petitioner's case under Order 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title in the suit land in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sapahar in the District of Noagaon, being Other Class Suit No. 81 of 1986. 

 5. Against the aforesaid ex-parte judgment dated 17.7.94 the petitioner filed an application under Order 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for re-hearing the appeal alleging inter alia that 17.7.94 was fixed for hearing of the appeal beyond his knowledge and his engaged Advocate and as such he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the appeal was called on for hearing, where on Misc. Case No. 91 of 1994 was started. 

 6. Opposite party Nos. 1-3 contested the aforesaid Misc. Case by filing written objection denying all material allegations of the application and contended inter alia that since the learned Subordinate Judge decided the appeal on merit by the impugned judgment dated 17.7.94 there is no scope for rehearing of the appeal. 

 7. At the trial the petitioner examined one witness and the contesting opposite parties examined none witness in support of their respective cases. The learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned order dated 18.7.96 dismissed Misc. Case No. 91 of 1994 on contest. Being aggrieved, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 8. Mr. S.N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the learned Subordinate Judge on a palpable erroneous view of law regarding the provision of Order 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure dismissed the petitioner's case and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 11. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before me the impugned order. It is found from the impugned order itself that 17.7.94 was fixed for hearing the appeal beyond the knowledge of the petitioner. The clear case of the petitioner is that he had no knowledge about the fixing of date of hearing of the appeal on 17.7.94 as a result of which he could not appear in the Court when the appeal was called for hearing on 17.7.94. It is thus that the petitioner was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the appeal was called for hearing on 17.7.94 and allowed ex-parte in his absence. 

 12. Order 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure gives ample power to the appellate Court to re-hear the appeal if the Court is satisfied that notice of the appeal was not served upon the respondent or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when that appeal was called on for hearing. The only point for consideration before a Court in deciding an application under Order 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure, is whether the applicant was pre-vented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the impugned judgment was passed ex-parte, no matter the judgment was delivered on merit. Ex-parte disposal of an appeal on merit is by itself no ground to refuse a relief under 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure when the applicant proves his case of prevention by sufficient cause. The view taken the learned Subordinate Judge that since he delivered the judgment on merit, there is no scope for rehearing the appeal is evidently wrong and arbitrary in view of the provision of Order 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same has indeed, occasioned failure of justice. 

 15. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 18.7.96 passed by the learned 1st. Co.urt of Subordinate Judge, Noagaon is set aside and Miscellaneous Case No. 91 of 1994 of the said Court under Order 41 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure is allowed, the impugned judgment dated 17.7.94 allowing Title Appeal No. 223 of 1988 is also set aside and the appeal is restored to its original file and number. The learned Subordinate, Judge, Noagaon is directed to re-hear Title Appeal No. 223 of 1988 according to law. 

 16. In view of the fact that this is a very old case, it is necessary in the interest of justice that the appeal be disposed of with utmost expediency. The learned 1st Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Noagaon is hereby directed to dispose of Title Appeal No. 223 of 1988 within 3 months from the dated of receipt of this order.
